          WSL Match Predictions
        
      
                          
                      Oct 1, 2026
          
                      Patric Ridge / Author, Jordan Collins / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
With the help of the Opta supercomputer, we provide our WSL match predictions for Matchday 5 of the 2026-27 season.
The Women’s Super League table is starting to take shape after the first four matches of the season.
Reigning champions Manchester City are the only team with a 100% record still intact after four straight wins to open the campaign.
Behind them, Chelsea and Tottenham are the only other teams yet to taste defeat, while London City Lionesses are also within touching distance of the top.
Arsenal have made a stuttering start, which was compounded by a 1-0 loss to Chelsea last time out, and things do not get any easier as they travel to City this weekend.
Things were more positive for Manchester United, who held out for their first league win under Eva Olid last time out, moving up the table and leaving four clubs without a victory.
So, who will come out on top in the WSL this weekend? We have a look at the Opta supercomputer’s Matchday 5 predictions.
The weekend’s action begins on Saturday, with Manchester United and Liverpool both looking to build on morale-boosting wins against West Ham and Everton, respectively.

Gareth Taylor (81) is aiming to join former United boss Marc Skinner (82) with the second-most managerial wins in WSL history – only Emma Hayes (151) has recorded more – and our predictive model gives that a 17.3% chance of happening.
As it stands, United are heavy favourites to take all three points at 63.2%, given they have won four of their five WSL home matches against the Reds (L1).
United have conceded in each of their last 11 home league games, which will give Liverpool hope of earning consecutive WSL wins for the first time since March 2025 under Amber Whiteley.
Despite a 19.5% chance of a draw, there has never been a stalemate between these teams in the competition in nine previous meetings (six United wins, three Liverpool victories).
It has been a tough start to the season for Aston Villa, who have gone winless in their four games (D2 L2), leading to Natalia Arroyo’s dismissal on Tuesday.
Brian Sørensen is in interim charge and will be in the dugout when Villa host Crystal Palace on Sunday. The hosts are the favourites to win, with a 45.3% win likelihood to Palace’s 27.8%.

Villa could go winless across their opening five matches of a WSL campaign for the third time (after 2023-24 and 2024-25), but they have won three of their last five league meetings with Palace (D1 L1).
Palace, meanwhile, have lost just one of their opening four league matches this term (W1 D2) – the fewest defeats of any promoted side at this stage of a single WSL campaign.
But both of their away games have finished in draws, and at 26.9%, this match is one of the most likely stalemates of the weekend.
Two teams still searching for their first win go head-to-head at the Amex, with Brighton and Charlton Athletic desperate for their victory.

Charlton are the only team still without a point – they could become the third team to lose their first five matches in the competition after Yeovil Town (first seven in 2017) and Leicester City (first nine in 2021-22).
But Brighton are also winless in their last seven WSL games (D4 L3). Only once before have they endured a longer such streak: nine between November 2022 and April 2023.
